name: FSFFL Reporting Layer
delivery_policy: For supported FSFFL analytical queries, interpret the raw workflow output conversationally and attach a standardized plain-English PDF. User-facing reports must lead with football meaning and decisions; technical field names and implementation details stay in the source JSON or footer unless a short explanation is necessary.

rules: charts only when they materially improve comprehension
define any unavoidable technical term in one sentence
never truncate user-facing prose with ellipses
every material number must include a comparison, scale, rank, baseline, or plain-language interpretation
decision reports must explain why the recommendation follows from the evidence
when alternatives exist, explain why the preferred option is better
page count may grow when needed to preserve context and narrative

automatic_report_pack.player_dossier: generated on demand for the queried player
automatic_report_pack.roster_decision: generated on demand from the queried Decision Lab scenario

numeric_context_policy: show league rank or percentile when available
show relative size versus assets surrendered or relevant baseline for value deltas
translate score magnitude into plain-language significance
never present an internal score without explaining what a higher or lower value means
roster_context_policy: connect recommendations to current optimized lineup access
connect incoming players to position need and roster weakness when supported
identify when outgoing players are blocked from the starting lineup or are depth-only assets
explain shifts from surplus positions to weak positions
use current competitive-window and simulator context when relevant
never infer a player will start unless an authoritative lineup output supports it
